articles.title: Fantasy Football Trade Tips: Keep the candle burning for Zay Flowers — help is on the way
articles.summary: Fantasy Football analyst Justin Boone offers up his advice for buying and selling as we head into Week 10.
articles.body:
Creating realistic trade offers that lead to a deal being accepted is always challenging. Throughout the season, Justin Boone will be publishing his rest-of-season trade value charts, which you can use as a guide to help make moves and manage your roster.

Below he highlights some of the players you should be buying or selling, before their value shifts in the coming weeks.

The arrival of Jacoby Brissett doesn't cure everything that's wrong with the Ravens, but it does give Flowers a chance to get back to producing at a high level. Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle had Flowers putting up elite stat lines and, if it wasn't for Lamar Jackson's injuries, we'd likely have witnessed a career year from the 26-year-old wideout. In addition to Brissett providing veteran quarterback play, Flowers will also benefit from one of the 10 easiest fantasy receiver schedules the rest of the way. That includes favorable matchups in the next three weeks with the Chargers, Panthers and Texans.

Be mindful that Flowers still has a bye week looming in Week 13, so you might want to look elsewhere if you're desperate for wins to stay in the playoff mix. Otherwise, you can target Flowers as a borderline low-end WR1/high-end WR2 with Brissett.

There have been a lot of concerns about Parker Washington's rest-of-season outlook, since he's been held under 65 yards in five of his last six games.

The issue isn't with Washington's talent, but the Jaguars' success. With Jacksonville opening up big leads most weeks, the team has been able to lean on their rushing attack and eventually sit their starters late in contests.

However, let's not get too cute with our projections and fail to recognize that Washington will be a part of the offense that's building these leads. Even in a rain-soaked game against the Ravens last week, Washington earned seven targets and posted 61 yards and a touchdown.

The Jags' receivers also have a top-10 fantasy schedule for the remainder of the season, including two games against the Titans in the next three weeks. Tennessee is allowing the most fantasy points to wideouts. Washington also has a friendly playoff slate with the Texans, Cowboys and Commanders — three of the top 11 most generous defenses to the position.

Washington remains a strong fantasy WR2 with WR1 upside.

Basically everyone in the Bills' passing attack can be considered a buy-low after a primetime brawl with Brian Flores' defense. Few pass-catchers come away with quality production in their matchup with the Vikings unit, and Moore was no exception, managing just 36 yards on four touches.

However, it's worth noting that Moore has posted stat lines of 5-100-1, 6-67-0 and 4-82-1 in the three games where he's played at least 60% of the snaps for Buffalo. Injuries have limited him in several contests, but the upside as Josh Allen's No. 1 target is obvious if Moore can stay healthy moving forward.

This is the time to acquire Moore, following an injury-riddled first half of the season, as well as a bad matchup and disappointing box score against Minnesota. The veteran will be a strong fantasy WR2 if he avoids the blue medical tent.

This move is for fantasy managers who are comfortably locked into a playoff spot, since Jacobs is set to miss time after undergoing surgery on a fractured finger. Initial reports said the veteran would miss a maximum of three weeks, but Matt LaFleur left the door open for a possible stint on injured reserve.

Over the next three weeks, the Packers get the Vikings, then a bye before facing the Rams. That's two bad matchups sandwiched around a week he was going to miss regardless. After that stretch, Green Bay has the easiest fantasy schedule for running backs, with the Saints, Bills, Dolphins, Bears and Texans.

Jacobs wasn't excelling from an efficiency standpoint with his touches, but was a solid fantasy RB2 thanks to volume and TD scoring. Given that list of opponents, he'll be an asset when he returns just in time for the fantasy postseason.

Prescott is the QB8 in fantasy points per game, but has only finished as a top-8 option in weekly scoring at his position twice in nine outings. While that makes him a fine low-end QB1 option, managers with championship aspirations need to set their sights higher.

One reason for that is Prescott's schedule once we reach December. The Cowboys will take on the Seahawks, then have an extremely late bye week, before dealing with the Rams and Jaguars in the first two weeks of the fantasy playoffs.

Bottom line, you aren't going to feel confident starting Prescott at any point during that month. It's time to move on and make alternative arrangements at quarterback.

Though Collins remains the unquestioned No. 1 receiver in Houston, C.J. Stroud's willingness to spread the ball around has led to reduced targets for his top option.

Collins has been limited to five targets or less in each of his last three games, after earning at least seven in his first three appearances. He's also finished outside the top 30 wideouts in three straight contests, before a touchdown helped him to a WR16 result in Week 9.

This all boils down to Collins falling into the fantasy WR2 range after being drafted as a WR1. While spike-weeks will surely occur, it's hard to project Collins as a top-12 fantasy starter the rest of the way. You should be trying to package him with a smaller piece and get RB1- or WR1-value in return.

Prior to the Titans' Week 9 bye, Pollard was the hottest runner in the league with back-to-back top-three fantasy RB results. The veteran totaled 155 yards and three touchdowns against the Browns, then hit the Bengals up for 137 yards and two scores a week later.

Hopefully he enjoyed those performances and the week off that followed, because the degree of difficulty is about to be turned up significantly on the Titans' rushing attack.

Tennessee has to face a surging Jaguars defense that just added a trio of starters before the trade deadline. Jacksonville was already the second toughest matchup for fantasy backs. Dating back to last year, Pollard managed just 63 and 65 scoreless yards, respectively, in his two encounters with this group.

Pollard also has negative fantasy matchups remaining against the Commanders (Week 13), Lions (Week 14) and Steelers (Week 17). Given the uncertainty that already exists around the Titans offense, it would be wise to move Pollard before he returns to reality.

Corum has scored double-digit fantasy points in five consecutive games and is the RB15 during that stretch. However, it's safe to wonder whether he'll be able to maintain that level of production with the receiving corps decimated by injuries.

Puka Nacua will be joining Davante Adams on IR and Terrance Ferguson is still a week or two away from getting back in the lineup. That leaves the Rams severely lacking in the pass-catcher department.

Corum should be fine for his matchup this week with the Cardinals, who are also banged up. Unfortunately after that, he has a bye week, followed by some tougher matchups like the Chiefs (Week 13), 49ers (Week 14), Seahawks (Week 16) and Buccaneers (Week 17).

As the No. 2 back in the offense behind Kyren Williams, Corum is dependent on competitive game scripts. His limited receiving role could cause him to spend more time on the sidelines if the Rams struggle while Nacua is out.

Sadly, we may have seen the best stretch of the season from Corum already, which is why you want to cash in while his value is at its peak.

articles.title: Frankie Muniz Released from Hospital After Race Car Crash at Daytona During Practice Lap
articles.summary: Actor and race car driver Frankie Muniz has been released from the hospital after initially being admitted following a car crash, he said in a statement via Bob Pockrass of Fox Sports:
articles.body:
Actor and race car driver Frankie Muniz has been released from the hospital after initially being admitted following a car crash, he said in a statement via Bob Pockrass of Fox Sports:

"I am disappointed I won't be able to take part in Ford's Proud to Honor event tonight. I was looking forward to honoring the service of our veterans and racing against these other amazing drivers. I am a little sore, but my Mustang did its job in protecting me. I want to thank everyone at Ford Racing, Daytona International Speedway and the staff here at the hospital. I especially want to thank everyone who has reached out and for all the prayers."I am disappointed I won't be able to take part in Ford's Proud to Honor event tonight. I was looking forward to honoring the service of our veterans and racing against these other amazing drivers. I am a little sore, but my Mustang did its job in protecting me. I want to thank everyone at Ford Racing, Daytona International Speedway and the staff here at the hospital. I especially want to thank everyone who has reached out and for all the prayers."

Muniz was hospitalized after crashing during a practice lap ahead of Wednesday's Veterans Day Classic at Daytona International Speedway, according to Team Reaume and Entertainment Weekly .

"Frankie Muniz was involved in an incident while practicing for today's Proud to Honor event at Daytona International Speedway," Team Reaume said in a statement. "He was transported to a local medical facility for further evaluation. He is awake and alert."

Daytona was not open to the public at the time of Muniz's crash, according to Entertainment Weekly . A photo shared by Entertainment Weekly showed damage to the No. 30 Mustang Dark Horse R he was slated to drive.

Wednesday's race was set to feature Ford competitors racing in honor of the six military branches. Muniz was slated to represent the U.S. Air Force alongside Austin Cindric.

Muniz was involved in a crash earlier this season during an April NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series race at Bristol Motor Speedway but walked away from the incident.

Best known in his acting career for starring in Malcolm in the Middle, Muniz first raced in 2004 and restarted his career in 2021.

He competed full-time with Rette Jones Racing in ARCA Menards Series in 2023, then took over driving Reaume's No. 33 Ford in the Truck Series in 2025.

Muniz skipped multiple races from the Truck Series in October while winning the 2026 GT4 America Am championship title with co-driver Tyler Stone.

His best race of this NASCAR season came with a 12th-place finish at Talladega Superspeedway Oct. 23. Muniz most recently placed 25th at Martinsville Speedway Oct. 30.

The Veterans Day Classic, which features a 15-minute qualifying session followed by a 30-minute, 12-turn race, is scheduled to air at 8 p.m. ET on USA Networ

articles.title: Xavier gets tough early-season test against Mississippi State
articles.summary: After a 3-0 start, Xavier gets a litmus test matchup against Mississippi State in the Greenbrier Tip-Off Nov. 13.
articles.body:
If you're a Xavier men's basketball fan, the last month has been bliss as the Musketeers returned to the court with a revamped roster under second-year head coach Richard Pitino .

In October, Xavier won all three of its exhibition games in different ways. In November, Xavier has done what a team with NCAA Tournament aspirations should do against its buy-game opponents, winning by an average of 37.7 points after Tuesday's 100-55 blowout of Detroit Mercy.

But now, the rubber is about to meet the road. Four of Xavier's next five games are against another high-major program, beginning with an SEC test against Mississippi State in the Greenbrier Tip-Off in the cozy confines of Colonial Hall in West Virginia.

"We're gonna really learn a lot about ourselves," Pitino said.

Photos: Detroit Mercy Titans at Xavier Musketeers, 11/10

Xavier's defensive scouting report starts with Josh Hubbard

In an era full of change, Josh Hubbard has been a constant in Starkville. In Monday's win over Jackson State, Hubbard became the fourth player in program history to score 2,000-plus points. He's only 142 points away from becoming the school's all-time leading scorer.

Last season, Hubbard ranked 10th in the nation in scoring at 22.1 points per game. In three buy games thus far, Hubbard is shooting 56.3% from 3-point range and is averaging 18 points and five assists.

Whether it's slowing down Hubbard or making sure Mississippi State's complementary pieces don't beat you, Xavier will have its hands full against a team that has averaged 95.3 points through three games while shooting 52.4% from the field.

Can Xavier continue its success getting to the rim?

Xavier wants to improve on its shooting percentages from 3-point range and at the charity stripe, but the Musketeers are getting to the rim and finishing at a high percentage.

Xavier is No. 7 in KenPom in two-point shooting and boasts the seventh-tallest lineup in college basketball. That size can be advantage against a smaller Mississippi State rotation.

We'll see if Xavier gets Mike Nwoko involved early in the post. The LSU transfer is shooting 73.9% so far this season, helping Xavier rack up 160 points in the paint over three games.

Xavier is off to a stellar defensive start, holding three consecutive opponents under 30% shooting. They'll try to force misses against Mississippi State, but the Muskies need to make them one-and-done possessions. The Bulldogs haven't missed a lot, but when they do, they're creating second-chance opportunities with 48 offensive rebounds thus far. Mississippi State's offensive rebounding percentage is fourth in the country, per KenPom.

Xavier has had two great games on the glass, but Eastern Michigan's size and physicality led to a 39-33 advantage on the glass Nov. 6. Xavier won't be able to afford those lapses in the rebounding battle.

Tip : 9 p.m., Friday, Nov. 13 at Colonial Hall at The Greenbrier Resort (1,200)

Ratings : Xavier is No. 40 in KenPom and Mississippi State is No. 55.

History : Mississippi State has won four of five all-time matchups. Xavier's lone win over Mississippi State was in the second round of the 2004 NCAA Tournament in Orlando, Florida.

Head coach : Chris Jans (79-59 at Mississippi State, fifth season)

Overview : Like Xavier, Mississippi State is 3-0 after three buys games. The Bulldogs allowed 88 points in their season-opening win over Tennessee Tech. They responded by giving up a combined 101 points on just 32.7% shooting (35-for-107) in blowout wins over Northwestern State and Jackson State.

Head coach : Richard Pitino (18-18 at Xavier, second season)

Xavier vs. Mississippi State final score prediction

It'll be interesting to see what the environment is like in such a small arena. Xavier's defensive intensity and height advantage carries the Musketeers to a 4-0 start: Xavier 75, Mississippi State 70

articles.title: Kaden Honeycutt Pays Tribute to NASCAR Legends In Championship Speech
articles.summary: Kaden Honeycutt paid tribute to late NASCAR legends during his championship speech.
articles.body:
NASCAR Truck Series champion Kaden Honeycutt put quite a finishing touch on his championship speech at Tuesday night's NASCAR Awards in Miami. The driver of the No. 11 Tricon Garage Toyota recognized Dale Earnhardt, Greg Biffle, and Kyle Busch in his last line of his speech.

Honeycutt outlasted Layne Riggs to win his first NASCAR Truck Series championship. Entering the final race, Riggs trailed Honeycutt by 20 points. However, the challenge for the title ended as quickly as it started after Riggs suffered two separate tire failures, putting him multiple laps down.

Honeycutt overachieved in the championship race as he took the checkered flag at Homestead-Miami Speedway. It was Honeycutt's first career title and second straight for Tricon Garage. The team won the title with Corey Heim in 2025.

Kaden Honeycutt Finishes Speech Honoring NASCAR Legends

As Honeycutt finished his championship speech in front of a packed house in Miami, he had three more things to say. Each of his lines recognized three late NASCAR champions, Dale Earnhardt, Greg Biffle, and Kyle Busch.

"Lastly, I want to leave off with three lines. Do it for Dale, be like Biff, and race for Rowdy. Thank you guys," Honeycutt said.

Earnhardt, a seven-time Cup Series champion and 76-time race winner, died in a last-lap crash in the 2001 Daytona 500. Biffle, a champion in the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series and Truck Series, and Busch, a two-time Cup Series champion, shockingly perished within the last calendar year.

On December 18, 2025, Biffle, his wife, Cristina, his two children, Emma and Ryder, and three others were killed in a plane crash in Statesville, North Carolina. Biffle was 55 years old.

On May 21 of this year, Busch died in a Charlotte hospital after complications of pneumonia. He was 41 years old.

It was a touching statement by Honeycutt to recognize the greats NASCAR has lost in recent memory and a slogan that many fans render at the racetracks and on social media.

A Look at Kaden Honeycutt's 2026 Championship-Winning Season

Entering the 2026 NASCAR Truck Series season, Kaden Honeycutt had yet to score a win in the series. By the end of the campaign, Honeycutt had captured five victories and the 2026 championship.

Honeycutt scored his first career Truck Series win at Watkins Glen International. The driver of the No. 11 backed it up with a win at Richmond in August.

In the Chase, Honeycutt earned victories at Kansas, Phoenix, and Homestead-Miami Speedway. With that performance, the 23-year-old out of Willow Park, Texas became a NASCAR champion.

Honeycutt will return to the No. 11 truck for the 2027 season.

articles.title: Matthew Stafford a full participant Wednesday; Myles Garrett limited
articles.summary: Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (right elbow) had full participation on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (right elbow) had full participation on Wednesday.

Stafford went on the injury report with his injury a week ago, but he played all 75 offensive snaps in Sunday's win over the Commanders.

Outside linebacker Myles Garrett (knee) was limited after playing 37 of 62 defensive snaps in his return Sunday, when he had three sacks. He had not played since Week 1 after undergoing arthroscopic surgery on his knee the following week.

Offensive lineman Steve Avila (hamstring), wide receiver Puka Nacua (knee/toe), cornerback Trent McDuffie (back), safety Kam Curl (toe) and tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) did not practice.

Tight end Davis Allen (oblique), tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs) and long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle) were limited.

How has that close loss impacted the Cougars?

Four others, though, have the Cougars playing in the Alamo Bowl.

Defending Big 12 champion Texas Tech, after surviving a high-scoring thriller against West Virginia last week, is also receiving some CFP love, with four of those projections pinning the Red Raiders in the playoff.

articles.title: Rs 50 lakh debt, visa nightmare: Teenage Indian chess prodigy risks losing US scholarship
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Last June, seventeen-year-old Md Imran was in Bratislava, Slovakia, when an incident turned his European chess campaign into a nightmare.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Last June, seventeen-year-old Md Imran was in Bratislava, Slovakia, when an incident turned his European chess campaign into a nightmare. As previously reported on TimesofIndia.com, he lost his passport, his phone, money and several personal belongings. More than just his valuables, he had lost something far more important, his valid US F-1 visa and Schengen visa.Stranded in a foreign country, with no easy way to get home or continue his journey, the young Indian chess player suddenly found himself fighting a battle that had little to do with the 64 squares. But Imran, hailing from Andhra Pradesh, refused to let the setback end his journey.In the days and weeks that followed, he produced two consecutive Grandmaster (GM) norms, bringing him within touching distance of the coveted Grandmaster title.Yet, four months after that incident, Imran is back in India, facing a different kind of situation, which includes an unresolved US visa crisis, mounting family debt, and the possibility of losing a full university scholarship that could change his life.The teenager, who became an International Master (IM) in 2025, has already deferred his admission to the University of Texas at Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV) in Brownsville, Texas, from Fall 2026 to Spring 2027.His new university orientation is scheduled for January 19, 2027. If he cannot secure his US F-1 visa before then, he risks losing the scholarship altogether.For a teenager who has spent years travelling across continents to chase his Grandmaster dream, the next few months could prove decisive.The Bratislava incident that changed everythingThe consequences of losing his passport in Bratislava were particularly severe because it contained both his valid US F-1 visa and his Schengen visa, which was valid until October 31.He eventually managed to obtain a replacement passport from the Indian Embassy in Budapest on June 29 and returned to India on July 6. But coming home did not mean the troubles were over."The very next day, on July 7th, I applied for a new Schengen visa for Hungary. This marked my 13th attempt at applying for a Schengen visa," Imran told TimesofIndia.com.Despite having competed extensively in Hungary over the previous two years, and having previously received a one-year multiple-entry visa from the same consulate, Imran was granted only a three-month visa, valid from July 18 to October 31.The decision left him frustrated, particularly when he knew fellow players who had received visas valid for two to five years in far fewer attempts."It sounded completely ridiculous, especially when I know many friends who have received 2- to 5-year validity visas in just their 2nd to 5th attempts. I truly don't understand what's wrong with my case," he added.For a young professional chess player, travelling back to India solely to process visas means more than another appointment and a few documents."Flying back to India solely for visa processing costs an exorbitant amount of time and heavy money on flight tickets, on top of the constant re-application hurdles," he added.A university dream on holdEven amid the uncertainty, Imran had already earned two norms in closed round-robin tournaments and was chasing his final open Swiss GM norm to complete the requirements for the Grandmaster title.His original plan was to continue competing in Europe, secure the remaining norm and return to India in time to obtain a US visa and attend UTRGV's Fall 2026 student orientation on August 23. But the US visa appointment never materialised."I waited in Europe and tried for a U.S. appointment all the way through August, September, and October. Unfortunately, despite trying every single day for four months since the June incident, I still have not secured an appointment," he said.With the August university deadline passing, he had little choice but to defer his admission to Spring 2027.His scholarship remains at stake. If he cannot make it to the university by the January 19 orientation, he could lose the financial support that would help him pursue higher education alongside his chess career.Between July and October, he competed in over ten events. However, only three were strong open tournaments where he had a realistic opportunity to secure his final GM norm.The remaining events were regular prize-money opens and round-robin competitions that helped him stay active.The three major opportunities were also poorly spaced, with two tournaments scheduled back-to-back between August 8 and 23, followed by the final one from October 3 to 11.It was a relentless schedule, made even harder by the uncertainty surrounding his university admission and his inability to secure a US visa appointment.The pressure eventually took its toll on the chessboard."Under the intense psychological pressure of the missing norm and my crumbling U.S. visa situation, my performance dipped. I suffered an insane rating decline despite relentless fighting spirit. Completely exhausted and under immense stress, I flew back home on October 12," Imran, who had a peak rating of 2503 and is now rated 2477, revealed.A family stretched to its financial limitsImran's father is a police officer, while his mother is a homemaker. Coming from a middle-class background, the family has had to stretch its resources to support his international chess career.Playing professionally in Europe costs between Rs 1.5 lakh and Rs 3 lakh every month. The expenses include flights, visas, accommodation, tournament entry fees, food and travel between countries.The family has reportedly accumulated loans of around Rs 40-50 lakh to finance his career. The June incident in Slovakia added another unexpected financial burden, with the loss of his passport, phone and other valuables."My father has supported me with everything he possibly can, stretching himself to the absolute limit, but it's falling short over time," Imran further noted. "I built my chess career entirely through my own hard work without formal high-end coaching."Imran has approached the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister's Office and other political leaders, seeking financial assistance through state sports incentive schemes. However, his requests have so far gone unanswered.A race against timeWith his three-month Schengen visa approaching its October 31 expiry, Imran returned to the Hungarian Consulate in Mumbai on October 16 for another application. It was his 14th Schengen visa application.This time, he received an emergency appointment and was granted a one-year visa on October 24. While the longer validity offers some relief, it was still shorter than the five-year visa he had hoped to secure given his extensive tournament and travel history across Europe.At least one part of the travel crisis had eased. But the bigger problem remained untouched, his US F-1 visa. With January 19, 2027, approaching, Imran now needs to secure an appointment and complete the visa process in time to join UTRGV and protect his scholarship.One final Grandmaster normDespite everything, Imran is preparing to return to Europe for another demanding tournament circuit in the hope of securing his final GM norm. He is scheduled to fly back on November 19, with four events lined up across Portugal, Spain and Sweden:Funchal Open, Portugal: November 26 to December 2El Llobregat Open, Spain: December 3 to 8Sunway Sitges Chess Festival, Spain: December 12 to 22Rilton Cup, Stockholm, Sweden: December 27 to January 5The schedule leaves little room for rest. More importantly, he is desperately hoping to secure a US visa appointment before leaving India on November 19."My life is currently at a critical crossroads. Between the heavy financial debts of playing professional chess, the constant struggle to secure my final GM norm, and the looming threat of losing my U.S. university scholarship at the University of Texas at Rio Grande Valley if I can't resolve my visa crisis by Spring 2027, the situation is completely overwhelming," he concluded.For a teenager who has done so much to keep his dreams alive, the question is whether the support he needs will arrive before January 19.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: War of words between Michigan Wolverines-Oregon Ducks heats up as Dan Lanning responds to criticisms
articles.summary: Kyle Whittingham took aim at Oregon's $50M+ NIL spending, and Dan Lanning fired back with a pointed jab at Michigan's costly coaching buyouts.
articles.body: Well, the Big Ten Conference might not be having the best season on the field, but off the field? The drama just keeps brewing. And of all teams, this time it involves ... the Michigan Wolverines and Oregon Ducks? The two teams, both having varying degrees of disappointing results thus far in 2026, face off on Saturday in Eugene, and despite the lack of history between the two programs, there's some bad blood rapidly brewing. It started thanks to already-embattled Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham. His first season in Ann Arbor has been, to put it mildly, well below expectations. While at Utah, the 66-year-old was known for being a calm, steady voice of leadership who seemed to always win the games he needed to win. The Utes punched well above their historical weight, and his penchant for stability. Whittingham was in Salt Lake City for 32 years, looked like a perfect fit for a Michigan program coming off years of turmoil. MICHIGAN'S NEW HEAD COACH POURS COLD WATER ON OHIO STATE RIVALRY: 'HATE IS A STRONG WORD' But the Wolverines' struggles started almost immediately. Whittingham dismissed the importance of the Michigan-Ohio State rivalry game, which put him on the wrong foot with most fans. Then the Wolverines required some questionable clock management from the replay review crew to pull out a miraculous 13-12 comeback win over Western Michigan. They rebounded to beat Oklahoma the following week, but lost to Iowa, Minnesota and Indiana from late September to late October. Their offense has been dismal all season, culminating in an awful 15-6 loss to Michigan State last on November 7. Instead of progressing in his second year as a starter, Bryce Underwood has ranged from disappointing to unacceptably bad. To the point where Whittingham benched him for backup Tommy Carr. All this has led to speculation and outright discussion around Michigan that boosters are preparing to pull together enough to buy Whittingham out after just one season. It also might explain why the normally uncontroversial coach is making headlines. MICHIGAN HIRED KYLE WHITTINGHAM TO FIX ITS MESS. INSTEAD, HE’S CREATED AN EVEN BIGGER ONE WITH WOLVERINES At a news conference ahead of this weekend's game, Whittingham praised Oregon head coach Dan Lanning, then took a shot at the Ducks' immense financial resources. "Outstanding football coach, defensive-minded coach. That’s his background. Tireless recruiter. He really does a great job recruiting, and it doesn’t hurt that you have $50+ million dollars at your disposal to, in essence outbid everybody," he said. "Not everybody, but a lot of people. But that’s not his fault. That’s a credit. I mean, that’s a credit to their program and their dedication and desire to win and the support they have. NIL is the name of the game in recruiting these days. It’s shifted so much. "It used to be the facilities you had and the tradition and all these other things, and now it’s, ‘Oh, this is all great, but these guys have a hundred grand more for me. So that’s a little bit of a factor to say the least. But not to take anything away from Dan, because he is an outstanding recruiter." Maybe there's some personal animus there, stemming from a fight between the two over a recruit or recruits? Regardless of the motivations though, Whittingham's right that the Ducks have significant advantages over other teams. Lanning though, unsurprisingly heard about it and, well, didn't love it. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE On Wednesday, Lanning said he had "nothing to say," then said something back. "I’ve got nothing to say to Coach Whit other than I think he’s an unbelievable coach, and I get it," he said. "They’re spending more of their money right now on their coaches that they’re letting go, so maybe it makes it hard to sign players. "But I know they’ve signed a couple of guys that we weren’t able to compete with what they decided to do, and maybe a lot of that money is tied up for them in another player. I don’t know. But Coach Whittingham is an unbelievable coach. He’s a Hall of Fame coach. I’ve got nothing but respect for him." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! That is definitely more than "nothing" to say! Both coaches are right about their fronthanded criticisms and backhanded compliments. Lanning deserves a ton of credit for helping keep Oregon's season (mostly) on the rails, recovering after losses to UCLA and Illinois to beat Northwestern and then Ohio State in Columbus. But the Ducks entered 2026 with championship aspirations in large part because of their very expensive roster. Yes, Dante Moore got hurt against USC, but that came after Oregon was thoroughly dismantled by Oklahoma State. And the money they have allowed them to sign Dylan Raiola, who started at Nebraska in 2025, as a backup. A luxury few other teams enjoy. They can outbid almost anyone if they really want to, or if they value a player more than the other team. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER So Whittingham is right that Lanning is a great recruiter, a very good head coach, and also has immense resources at his disposal. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Lanning is right to take a pot shot at Michigan's coaching staff problems, including the $10 million buyout owed to Jason Beck after just a few months of a three-year deal. And he's also right that Whittingham has been a great head coach his entire career. Just an incredible exchange of mutual praise, admiration, and sarcastic criticisms. Before the season, Oregon-Michigan seemed like one of the big games on the calendar, must-see TV for college football fans. Most of the shine is off, now that the Wolverines are buried and Oregon is clinging to hopes of reaching the Big Ten Conference Championship, but the war of words off the field has made the on-field game must-see TV all over again.

articles.title: El Langui cierra su primera temporada como internacional ¡con siete medallas!
articles.standfirst: El actor y rapero gana el bronce por equipos en la Copa del Mundo de Sao Paulo de boccia junto a Meñaka y Soliman en Sao Paulo. Laura Utrero y Alejandro Díaz, plata por parejas
articles.summary: El actor y rapero sube al tercer cajón del podio por equipos junto a Meñaka y Soliman en la última cita de la Copa del Mundo. Siete medallas en su primer año en la selección
articles.body: Juan Manuel Montilla, 'El Langui', acelera hacia los Juegos Paralímpicos de Los Ángeles 2028. El actor y rapero descubrió hace apenas dos años la boccia, el deporte paralímpico que algunos comparan con la petanca y que él denomina "el ajedrez de las bolas", y ya se ha consolidado no sólo entre los mejores jugadores de España sino también a nivel internacional. En sólo un año defendiendo la elástica de la selección, el de Pan Bendito ha conquistado siete medallas: cuatro individuales y tres por equipos. La última, precisamente, ha sido un bronce junto a Ainhoa Meñaka y Moha Soliman en la Copa del Mundo de Sao Paulo (Brasil), donde ya había ganado la plata individual. No ha sido la única medalla española esta jornada. Laura Utrero y Alejandro Díaz lograron la plata por parejas en BC3. Es el segundo metal de este color para la española. "Este bronce sabe muy bien porque, además de subirnos al podio, nos permite rascar unos puntos muy importantes para el ranking mundial por equipos. No olvidemos que la puntuación por equipos va por separado de la individual, así que también necesitábamos sumar y seguir escalando posiciones", dice El Langui a MARCA desde la ciudad brasileña. El madrileño se ha abonado al podio y en 2026 sólo se le ha resistido en su primer Mundial. El equipo BC1/BC2 logró clasificarse para las semifinales, donde se midieron a Kazajistán, una selección que está trabajando muy bien y que les puso las cosas realmente difíciles. España comenzó adelantándose, pero en el tercer parcial llegó el empate. "A partir de ahí fue un auténtico tira y afloja, bolita arriba, bolita abajo, hasta terminar empatados. Nos fuimos al desempate y, esta vez, la balanza cayó de su lado. Nos quedamos a las puertas de la final", analiza. Disputaron el bronce contra Francia, a la que acabaron ganando por 11-2. El equipo español salió muy sólido, concentrado y con las ideas muy claras. Desde el primer parcial marcó diferencias, poniéndose cuatro puntos por delante en el marcador. Y poco a poco alcanzaron los diez puntos y dejaron el partido prácticamente sentenciado al comienzo del sexto último parcial. Con esa ventaja, Francia ya no pudo remontar. "Estamos muy contentos con el trabajo realizado, con el esfuerzo de todo el equipo y con haber conseguido cerrar esta última competición internacional del año subiendo al podio. Tenemos la mirada puesta ya en 2027, un año importantísimo en el camino hacia los Juegos Paralímpicos de Los Ángeles 2028. Entramos en una etapa decisiva, donde cada entrenamiento, cada competición y cada punto van a contar muchísimo. Así que ahora más que nunca toca poner toda la carne en el asador, y dar ese último empujón fuerte para intentar estar donde todos soñamos", promete. Termina la temporada internacional y toca cambiar el chip porque este mismo fin de semana comienza la Liga autonómica. "Hay que seguir compitiendo, trabajando y disfrutando de este deporte", señala con la misma ilusión con la que empezó a practicarlo. El año pasado reconocía en MARCA que la boccia le había cambiado la vida. De pequeño soñaba con ser futbolista y debutar algún día en el Bernabéu. El balompié fue lo que le hizo superarse, buscar sus mañas para vestirse, levantarse cuando se caía o ducharse solo. Pero con 12 años, ya no podía jugar al nivel de sus amigos. Nada le motivaba y se refugió en el rap. Dejó el deporte a un lado. Después de 30 años sin practicar ninguno, descubrió la boccia y con esfuerzo y sacrificio, se ha consolidado en la élite. Y todo ello compaginándolo con las grabaciones, una obra teatral y conciertos. Su palmarés demuestra que los esfuerzos han merecido la pena.

articles.title: Darts player Katie Sheldon: Irish ace on brilliant Beau Greaves and how Littler Littler has inspired a boom in Ireland
articles.summary: Katie Sheldon talks about Beau Greaves and how Littler Littler is inspiring the next generation of players in Ireland; 'Beau 'n' Arrow' faces Littler at the Grand Slam of Darts; you can watch the tournament in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22
articles.body:
As one of the hottest prospects to come out of the Emerald Isle, Sheldon has already competed on the Women's Series and at the Women's World Matchplay held at the iconic Winter Gardens in Blackpool.

Currently working as a wire assembler, Sheldon has already become the World Masters girls' champion and a two-time WDF World Cup team winner.

"I keep saying that one goal of mine is to pick up a PDC title, so a Women's Series. And along with that, it's trying to qualify for the Women's World Matchplay," she told Sky Sports , having taken part in the Netflix 'Beat Luke Littler' challenge in which she was given the chance to win £501,000.

It wasn't to be for Sheldon over one leg against 'The Nuke', but she has bigger dreams of emulating brilliant Beau Greaves, who finished a dominant season on the PDC Women's Series by winning 17 out of 24 events.

The Doncaster thrower will be at the Grand Slam of Darts where she has been drawn with Luke Littler and Niels Zonneveld . She also secured her qualification for the world championship at Alexandra Palace alongside 'Beat Luke Littler' winner Fallon Sherrock, Gemma Hayter, 'The Lancashire Rose' Lisa Ashton, and Belgian-born Swedish darts player, Vicky Pruim.

'Beau 'n' Arrow' made history in April by becoming the first woman to win a PDC ranking title at Players Championship 11 in Milton Keynes, defeating three former world champions, Rob Cross, Gary Anderson and Michael Smith.

She has risen to 75th in the PDC Order of Merit with the youngster closing in on the world's top 64, an achievement that would have ramifications for her future in the Women's Series with female players who break into the top 64 globally and hold a Tour Card restricted from playing in the Women's Series.

"She's really a great talent, and she's pushed us all," said Sheldon. "I think her being there has actually brought the standard up.

"Her being there has been a massive help to all of the women to progress their game, but I think it would be a sad loss to the Women's Series when she's gone."

The success of two-time back-to-back world champion Littler has played a huge part in the surge of youth academies - not least in Ireland where Sheldon has seen a surge in interest.

She explained: "I think Luke has given everyone that [interest]. I think a lot of people have started picking up darts, but mainly youths.

"When I played youth darts in youth academies, there wasn't that many of us, a couple of lads, but the numbers are just through the roof now.

"We have a Dublin academy, and I think at the team event, there was 183 kids there at the weekend, just playing darts for their local teams and clubs, which is amazing for the sport.

"It's great to see the growth, and I think a lot of that is down to what Luke's done."

'People probably don't know what they're witnessing'

Despite his success, Littler has threatened to boycott certain tournaments after being booed and whistled by vociferous crowds - not least in the Netherlands and Germany.

Sheldon accepts "it's a hard one to take" for players as well as Littler, himself.

She said: "When he first came on the scene, everyone was bigging him up and it was great, but then you're turning up to tournaments and people are booing him.

"People probably don't know what they're witnessing at the minute. The standard of darts is just crazy.

"I think if you are a fan, you should be going there to enjoy it. Don't get me wrong, everyone loves singing the songs, but I think there should be just that level of respect for the players when they're playing because at the end of the day, this is their livelihood as well.

"They want to be trying to perform the best for the fans, and they probably can't do that with all the boos.

"It's one of those things he has to deal with, which is kind of sad to see."

Sky Sports remains the home of darts with the Grand Slam of Darts (November 14-22) and World Darts Championship (December 11-January 3) all live. Stream darts and more through NOW with no contract.

articles.title: Northern Ireland: Young duo Tom Atcheson and Ruairi McConville at the heart of Nations League's meanest defence
articles.summary: With Northern Ireland yet to concede a goal in the 2026-27 Nations League, young defenders Ruairi McConville and Tom Atcheson have been impressing for Michael O'Neill's side.
articles.body:
Across his two spells as Northern Ireland boss, Michael O'Neill has been blessed with no shortage of centre-back talent.

Jonny Evans, Aaron Hughes, Gareth McAuley and Craig Cathcart were mainstays of his first stint in charge - so much so that, in some of the biggest games of O'Neill's managerial career at Euro 2016, the quartet all started across a flat back-four.

Since returning to the job four years ago, O'Neill has switched to three at the back, with Sunderland duo Trai Hume and Dan Ballard providing an injection of Premier League quality in what remains a side largely drawn from the Championship and League One.

But with Hume, something of a Swiss army knife in the squad, covering the injured Conor Bradley on the right flank and even starting in centre midfield against Ukraine last month, and Ballard presently nursing an injured hamstring, change has been required through this Nations League campaign.

Despite those forced alterations in defence, the side go into their concluding Group B2 fixtures against Ukraine and Hungary top of their pool and the only side at any level of the competition yet to concede a goal.

At the heart of their defensive efforts have been Ruairi McConville and Tom Atcheson, two young centre-backs already described by their international manager as having "no ceiling" .

Birthdays and broken lamps - at home with the Charles brothers

NI can draw on strong club form in key window

At 21-years-old, Norwich City's McConville is the more senior of the pair.

Having been given his debut off the bench at home to Belarus two years ago this week, among the former Brighton man's early international assignments was trying to keep a rampant Alexander Isak in check during a 5-1 defeat by Sweden.

In the short time since he has looked an increasingly commanding figure, leading this Nations League group in clearances made with both head and boot.

"It would be unbelievable to keep that record for these last two games and go the whole of the campaign," he said of what is Northern Ireland's longest run without conceding a goal since 2017.

McConville notes that the streak is a team effort and product of collective work-rate, rather than just the defensive three alone.

"We're a team that works hard, a team that doesn't want to give anything up.

"We're confident in ourselves and we know that we're a good side."

It is McConville who has taken on the Ballard role in the middle of the defence for the past three games, with Atcheson on the right and Oxford United's Ciaron Brown, himself superb through the campaign so far, playing from the left.

On the developing understanding between an emerging unit, McConville added: "We're enjoying playing together.

"It's still early days together and we have to keep taking it game by game and doing what the gaffer tells us and the work on the training pitch.

"We don't have much time together when we're here [in international camp] so it's important to do all we can."

Watch on BBC iPlayer and BBC Two NI from19:15 GMT; Listen on BBC Sounds and BBC Radio Ulster; Watch, listen, live text and clips on BBC Sport app & website

After 16 caps, McConville is a relative veteran compared to Atcheson, who made his international bow in a friendly against Wales in March at a time when he had only four senior club starts to his name at Blackburn Rovers.

The most recent of those had come under O'Neill, then in a short stint as caretaker manager at the Championship club.

Clearly impressed by what he saw from the now 20-year-old at Ewood Park, Atcheson made his first Northern Ireland start against Guinea in June, a game in which he scored the winner with a fabulous flick before later being shown a red card.

Some 428 minutes into his international career, Atcheson is still to experience what it feels like to concede a goal.

The England-born defender feels Ballard "is definitely a big miss" to the side, but believes the squad's understanding of O'Neill's desired system is an asset to those who have starred during the Sunderland man's latest absence.

"I feel like everyone knows what they need to do, everyone knows their job, the details of the formation we play and system," he said.

"That's so key and I think that's why we're so solid defensively.

"It's a team thing, we're set up right, we're very on it all the time and everyone gives their all."
